Spain · 38°43′N 1°27′E

Formentera

Slow, salt-bleached, unrepeatable.

The place

A short ferry from Ibiza, and a different century. Formentera is flat, luminous and best explored by bicycle — with long lunches, shallow water and nowhere to be.

The island is small enough to know in a week and beautiful enough to return to for twenty years. The south has the famous water; the north has the quieter beaches and the best sunsets. Houses are low, white and built for outdoor living.

We keep a deliberately small Formentera portfolio: houses we have stayed in, close enough to the water to walk, and staffed by people who live on the island.

  • 01

    Ses Illetes

    The water everybody photographs, and it really is that colour. Go early, or go in September.

  • 02

    The interior

    Fig trees, dry stone walls and white roads — the island at bicycle speed.

  • 03

    The table

    Long lunches, fresh fish and a pace that makes dinner at ten feel early.

When to go

May — October

The island is at its best in June and September. August is busy; book ferries and restaurants well ahead.
